title: R' Abba bar Pappa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a Babylonian, a colleague of R' Zeira. We find this in Bava Metzia 43b, where R' Zeira said, 'When you go there (to the Land of Israel), make a detour by the Ladder of Tyre, and enter to R' Yaakov bar Idi and ask him whether he heard from R' Yochanan,' etc. Hyman says that he came to the Land of Israel in the time of R' Yochanan, for R' Zeira, who went up afterward, still found R' Yochanan. Hyman further reports that in Rosh Hashanah, beginning of chapter 4, he tells a story of R' Yochanan and Resh Lakish concerning what happened to them with Kahana. In Eruvin 63b he said, 'Yehoshua was punished only because —' and R' Yochanan said, 'This teaches,' etc. (all of this being the words of R' Abba bar Pappa). And in Bava Kamma 80a he said in the name of Rabbi Adda bar Pappa, and some say in the name of Rabbi Chiyya bar Pappa, and some say in the name of Rabbi Achah bar Pappa.

And in Shabbat 60b we find Rava bar Pappa, mentioned after R' Abbahu and before Rabbah bar R-H; but Hyman reports that the reading of the Rif there is Rafram bar Pappa.
Those who say in his name: we find R' Pinchas in Berakhot, beginning of chapter 1, and R' Pinchas HaKohen in Midrash Tehillim, ch. 32 (section 2).

The Gaon, author of Beit Va'ad LaChakhamim, wants to say that he is Abba Mar bar R-P, but Hyman rejects this as a mistake, arguing that the latter was later, and in his days all the academies of the Land of Israel had already been destroyed.

notes.text: Hyman’s supplied ascent wording is דמור; the named Davidson Bava Metzia43b text reads the Ladder of Tyre (דצור). The difference is noted rather than silently changing the Hebrew. RY in the chronology is Rabbi Yochanan, already named in the sentence; Rabbah bar Rav Huna is not Rabbah bar bar Chana. Hyman’s rejection of the later Abba Mar identification remains his judgment.

The whole saved William Davidson vocalized-Aramaic Bava Kamma80b scalar (376 characters) was checked against its raw SHA256, selector and actual edition metadata. It explicitly has Rabbi Acha bar Pappa reporting Rabbi Abba bar Pappa reporting Rabbi Adda bar Pappa; alternatively Rabbi Abba bar Pappa reporting Rabbi Chiyya bar Pappa reporting Rabbi Acha bar Pappa; alternatively Rabbi Abba bar Pappa reporting Rabbi Acha bar Pappa reporting Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa. All are bar Pappa and reporting direction is retained. These full titles support only the local names in this named scalar: they do not expand the heading or the earlier Eruvin parenthetical title, or prove the identities of the people in other passages. Hyman's shortened three alternatives remain his supplied wording; no missing links, Chanina continuation, mnemonic, legal teaching or verse is imported into the translated body. The supplied Bava Kamma פ. remains the conventional80a reading beside this digital80b comparison; the proposed body-locator replacement is not applied, and no Hebrew correction, print history or hold clearance is admitted. The earlier finite80a nonmatch remains a bounded historical digital nonmatch, not absence across a work or observed printed-page proof. The older Bava Metzia43b Ladder of Tyre claim and supplied Mor spelling remain distinct; that older witness was not freshly read whole this wake. Mor remains in the translation without replacing it with Tyre or claiming a place identity. The source heading and all unsupported abbreviated titles remain R'; the local Adda/Chiyya/Achah titles may be Rabbi because they occur explicitly in the selected Bava Kamma scalar. Zeira, Yaakov bar Idi, Yochanan, the earlier Abba, Abbahu and both Pinchas occurrences receive no title transfer from it. R-Z and R-Y contextually read as Zeira and Yochanan are inherited contextual expansions, not fresh passage bindings. The inherited Resh Lakish reading remains contextual. Hyman's Babylonian/colleague, arrival/Zeira chronology, and the surrounding first-person-plural WE FIND claims are preserved and attributed, without accepting chronology, genealogy or identity. WHEN you go, enter and ASK HIM WHETHER HE HEARD, the Israel parenthesis, ONLY punished BECAUSE incomplete dash, This teaches/etc, all three SOME SAY alternatives, and all reporting directions remain. BEFORE and AFTER in the Shabbat listing remain textual order, not chronology. Rava/Rafram bar Pappa remain distinct, and Hyman's reported Rif reading is uncollated. Rabbah bar R-H and Abba Mar bar R-P leave their initials unexpanded; the older Rav Huna, bar-bar-Chana and Rav/Rabbi Pappa expansions remain exact in history, not fresh Shabbat/Rif evidence. BEGINNING chapter4 RoshHashanah and BEGINNING chapter1 Berakhot remain contextual expansions of supplied רפ״ד/רפ״א; MidrashTehillim32 section2 and all other printed locators remain conventional, without fresh edition mapping. The Gaon's proposed Abba Mar identification and Hyman's definite THIS IS A MISTAKE rejection retain their force, as do LATTER/LATER/ALREADY/ALL academies in Israel: these are attributed competing claims, not admitted historical conclusions. Both original mixed notes and the current mixed note, all English histories and every root intermediate remain exact; no retirement or revision is applied. Only this qualification is appended and p001 remains held, with no publication, canonical source change or authority binding.

The whole printed notice is in volume I, p. 54. Its ascent reads דצור, Tyre, beside the frozen Hebrew דמור, Mor; the English follows the print as “Ladder of Tyre,” while the Hebrew and existing notes remain unchanged. The whole consulted Bava Metzia 43b passage also has the Ladder of Tyre, with Zeira asking Abba bar Pappa to ask Yaakov bar Idi what he heard from Yochanan. Hyman’s arrival and colleague conclusions remain his historical argument. The whole Bava Kamma 80b passage gives the longer chains Acha–Abba–Adda, Abba–Chiyya–Acha, and Abba–Acha–Chanina, all bar Pappa. Those links are not inserted into Hyman’s shortened alternatives; his supplied 80a locator remains beside this 80b comparison. Eruvin 63b has Abba bar Pappa’s Joshua teaching and the subsequent Yochanan explanation; that comparison does not independently establish Hyman’s claim about the attribution of the whole discussion. The exact Rosh Hashanah, Rif, Midrash Tehillim and Beit Va’ad passages have not been collated here. The bounded Shabbat 60a–b comparison did not recover the reported Rava/Rafram passage and does not establish absence. R-H and R-P remain unexpanded. The proposed Abba Mar identification and Hyman’s definite rejection, including “later,” “already” and “all” the academies, remain attributed competing historical claims. All existing notes are preserved verbatim.
